subject: AWS Private Offer — pricing bands & signoff authority
messages:
From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@cloudhealth.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@cloudhealth.io>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:18:00-04:00
Subject: AWS Private Offer — pricing bands & signoff authority

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers. We are starting to map procurement and approvals for a cross-division private offer and need some clarifications before we move to a PO. High-level asks:  

- Can you confirm recommended pricing bands for a 18–36 month term at these annualized spend buckets: <$200k, $200k–$500k, >$500k?
- Does Redwood support delegated signing authority so our procurement can sign a Marketplace private offer without exec-level signature for deals up to $250k?
- Any special co-sell paperwork or AWS tagging requirements for listing the product in our AWS account?

We also have two procurement contacts (copied) who will handle the PO template. If easier, feel free to send a proposed pricing sheet and an example Marketplace private offer flow.

Thanks,
Sofia Ramirez
Senior Cloud Architect — CloudHealth

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@cloudhealth.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T11:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — pricing bands & signoff authority

Sofia — thanks for the clear ask. Quick answers up-front, then next steps.

1) Pricing bands (indicative):
   - < $200k/yr: list pricing with 10% introductory discount
   - $200k–$500k/yr: 18%–22% off list depending on term and MC commitment
   - > $500k/yr: 25%+ (custom; requires Sales Ops approval)

2) Delegated signing: Redwood supports seller-side delegation for AWS Private Offers. We can accept a buyer-signed private offer if your procurement confirms delegated authority up to $250k. Anything above that typically needs revenue manager or CRO approval. We will need the delegation language/mail confirming buyer’s internal authorization to attach to the private offer request.

3) Co-sell / listing requirements: minimal tagging required (account ID & Deal ID), and you must enable the Private Offer with the correct product SKU. I attached a short checklist (mcp_requirements.pdf) and a pricing workbook (pricing_breakdown_CH-8421.xlsx) so you can pick a band.

Proposed next steps:
- Procurement to return your PO template + delegation confirmation (procurement@cloudhealth.io).
- We pull a Marketplace private offer draft and share DocuSign to parallel legal redlines.
- If you want a fixed 18-month term we can propose a stepped discount schedule (higher initial discount vs extended term).

Looping Vanessa and Marcus for approvals: Vanessa, Marcus — can you confirm whether the >25% band needs SalesOps/email escalation? Also confirm whether we can accept buyer delegation for up to $250k without legal attaching additional paperwork.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@cloudhealth.io>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-13T08:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — pricing bands & signoff authority

On Tue, Apr 12, 2027 at 11:05 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Proposed next steps:
> - Procurement to return your PO template + delegation confirmation (procurement@cloudhealth.io).

Quick internal note: approval thresholds we enforce today — please consider when positioning:
- Up to $250k: AE may accept buyer-delegated PO if procurement confirms authority in writing (email ok).
- $250k–$750k: requires RevOps (Lauren) verbal/email signoff and record in HubSpot.
- > $750k: requires Sales Director + Legal redline approved.

Marcus — please validate the >25% discount request; we typically route anything >22% to SalesOps for co-sell approval.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Procurement <procurement@cloudhealth.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@cloudhealth.io>
Date: 2027-04-14T13:02:00-04:00
Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — pricing bands & signoff authority

Vivek / Sofia,

Attached is CloudHealth's standard PO template (CloudHealth_PO_template.pdf). A few clarifications from our side:  

- We can issue a PO via AWS Marketplace private offer once Redwood confirms the SKU and the exact Marketplace line item description.
- Delegation: procurement can sign private offers up to $250k, but we require the buyer division head (Alex Moreno) to confirm delegated signatory authority in an internal email (we can forward once done).
- Term options: procurement prefers 12 or 36 month terms for budgeting; 18 month is unusual but acceptable if pricing is aligned to our budget cycle.
- Invoice cadence: prefer quarterly invoicing for multi-division contracts.

We will circulate the signed delegation note once Alex confirms.

Regards,
CloudHealth Procurement Team

Attachment: CloudHealth_PO_template.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Procurement <procurement@cloudhealth.io>, Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@cloudhealth.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-15T09:40:00-04:00
Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — pricing bands & signoff authority

Thanks — appreciated. Based on your comments, here is a concrete proposal we can push to a private offer draft:  

- Term: 18 months (we propose this as a midpoint to align deployment schedule).
- Pricing: Annualized list spend of $300k => 20% off list (year 1). Year 2 (final 6 months) billed pro-rata at the same effective rate. Total committed annualized spend locked for the term.
- Delegated signing: Redwood accepts procurement-signed Marketplace private offer up to $250k subject to CloudHealth email confirmation from the division head. Please send the delegation note when available.
- Invoicing: quarterly in arrears (Net 30).

Next steps:
- Procurement: confirm delegation email (procurement@cloudhealth.io) + return PO template populated with Redwood's company details and desired SKU line.
- We will prepare Marketplace private offer draft and send DocuSign (link below) to parallel legal review.

DocuSign (draft): https://www.docusign.com/embedded/abcdef-CH8421
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/CH-8421

If procurement is comfortable with the 18-month approach we will push for a private offer immediately.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@cloudhealth.io>, Procurement <procurement@cloudhealth.io>
Date: 2027-04-15T10:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — pricing bands & signoff authority

Vivek / team — I reviewed the numbers. Confirming: 20% on $300k annualized is acceptable under our standard co-sell concession for a first-year expansion. Anything heavier (25%+) will need SalesOps approval and a co-sell plan (with AWS rep engagement).

Action items from pricing:
- I'll lock SKU mapping and submit the Marketplace product descriptor so procurement can populate the PO line item correctly. Expect a separate attachment with suggested SKU and short description by EOD.
- Vanessa / Lauren: please note the RevOps routing if buyer later asks to extend to 36 months with higher discount.

Marcus Lin
Principal Pricing Analyst — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@cloudhealth.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@cloudhealth.io>, Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@cloudhealth.io>
Date: 2027-04-16T14:00:00-04:00
Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — pricing bands & signoff authority

Vivek / team — thanks for the clarity. A couple final items before we sign:  

- CloudHealth confirms delegation for procurement to sign up to $250k for this division. Procurement will forward the internal delegation note by EOD.
- For the Marketplace listing, can Redwood confirm the exact SKU we should reference so our procurement team populates the private offer correctly? Also confirm the line item will be billed as a single metered SKU and the invoice cadence quarter-in-arrears (Net 30).
- We prefer the 18-month term if you can confirm quarter billing and the 20% rate on the $300k band.

If you provide the SKU and I get the delegation note, procurement will prepare the PO and we can sign the DocuSign+private offer in parallel.

Alex Moreno
VP, Infrastructure — CloudHealth
